speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the implementation of home-based learning during the circuit breaker period (a) what is the total number of students returning to their schools during this period; (b) how do schools assess whether students have the necessary support at home to do home-based learning and, if not, will need to return to school; and (c) whether there have been requests from parents for students to attend school during this period which could not be acceded to and, if so, what are the reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The few who did not participate were largely on medical leave, and those who did not participate persistently were encouraged to return to school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Notwithstanding, schools have also identified a proportion of students who would benefit from returning to school during this period, based on their understanding of the student and his/her family circumstances, parents' requests, and referrals from social workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These would generally come under the following categories.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: First, students whose parents are in essential services and do not have alternative care-giving arrangements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These students can also access the limited services offered by school-based Student Care Centres, or SCCs, including students who were not previously enrolled in the SCCs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Second, students who face significant challenges learning at home, require face-to-face support or, for whom, a school environment is in the best interest of the student.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Schools proactively identified these students and encouraged them to return to school, by providing a welcoming environment and additional small-group activities such as non-contact sports and enrichment modules, while practising safe distancing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This has helped them to stay connected and engaged, and maintain a school-going routine.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Thirdly, students who do not have sufficient digital devices at home or needed Internet access to support home-based learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The numbers coming back to schools for this purpose has dropped significantly since, to a small group whose parents do not wish to loan for personal reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: If Members come across families who need devices, please refer them to the school, as we have more than enough to loan out.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The challenge has in fact been the opposite, where schools invite the student to come back to school, but the parents were reluctant over various reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Beyond the loan of devices, MOE and schools have also provided support to students and their families to facilitate participation in full HBL.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Teachers monitored their students’ learning and well-being through text messages, phone or video calls.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Resource kits are provided so parents can help supervise their children and reinforce their learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Through these various measures, we have been able to maintain high participation in HBL while at the same time enabling those with genuine need to return to school subject to the enhanced safe distancing measures in force during this period.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I just wanted to check a little bit more about the issues that some of the parents have been facing because we hear a lot of feedback that it is has been very challenging, even for the most savvy of parents to actually conduct HBL.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am just wondering whether schools and the Ministry have been receiving feedback about some of these challenges that parents are facing, and how are they supported in carrying out some of the HBL lessons at home.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The second thing I wanted to check on is the teachers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How are they coping with this because it is also not very easy for them managing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I think I heard feedback that some of them have challenges in ensuring the level of reception of the students, especially through online learning.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, how are teachers being supported in this?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Especially since a recent article mentioned about how some of the students needed support beyond just their lessons but also in terms of the counselling they need because the challenges their parents may be facing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, I am just wondering how are the teachers supported in all these, especially since some of them also are parents themselves and also have to handle HBL for their own kids.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That said, it has gone on much better than we had hoped but not without challenges.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Some of the challenges are obviously from the parents' view point: some had to get familiar with the resource kits, some had to learn how to use the software, others were okay with the resource kits and the software but they had to work from home or they had more than one child who was also doing home-based learning.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There were some, and for them this is particularly challenging if they had a child with special needs and other children who are also doing home-based learning.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, what the schools and the teachers have tried to do is to ensure that they maintained a contact with the parents, talked through the issues that the parents have and together tried to work at various solutions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And this is also bearing in mind that no two children are exactly alike.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Some have taken to the home-based learning very well but some others need more offline learning; and the parents have had to adjust and cope with that as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I rather suspect that the school holidays commencing tomorrow will be a welcome break for all.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With regard to teachers, here I really would like to salute the teachers for the tremendous effort that they made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Many of you do not see this behind the scenes but when HBL was first announced, the teachers had to come together very quickly to put together the packages and the resource kits.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What was heartwarming from this that we have learnt from the feedback from the schools, is that those teachers who were familiar with technology started to help those who were less familiar.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Some of the older ones who were very experienced teachers but not so familiar with technology were learning from some of the younger ones.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, altogether it was an experience where people shared their different knowledge; the teachers shared different resources; some of them were just putting together DIY kits, building on MOE resources that were available.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But altogether moving in the same direction with the sole purpose of making sure that the children were adequately equipped, and also trying to ensure that the parents were supported in this task of home-based learning.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And for the students who need support beyond lessons, obviously, the teachers also have been trying to engage them in other ways.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And for the ones who have other issues, the school counsellors and the social welfare officers have reached out to them, again, either by telephone calls, video calls, emails, but just trying to make sure that they stay in contact with the students so that they are supported.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And it is very heartening to know that the reply regarding students with special education needs as well.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I expect, as the Minister Lawrence had mentioned, in time there will be more information on who will be allowed to return midway during circuit breaker period.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But for now, can I ask the Minister to share MOE's experience with regard to perhaps students who are boarders or students who do not have strong family support at home and maybe might be in school hostels, for example.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are special concerns given to these students in terms of allowing them the support, bearing in mind that they might be in their room for a significant period of time without the family support that other children or other students may have in their home.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the children who are without family support, the teachers in the schools are especially mindful to make an extra effort for these students.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These students also have access to the limited services available.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I would just like to reassure the Member that every effort to ensure that these students are supported.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I do agree that HBL has given us all a very big learning curve during this period.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In short, I would like to ask MOE to consider an initiative to take stock of all these learnings, so that indeed we will be able to progress to the next level of e-learning, blended learning and so forth.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you have got to make sure you have the right mix.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You also want to make sure that you have a healthy mix.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there are actually many things that have come out of this and we should see this as an opportunity to learn, to derive new strategies and add that into the mix of things, as we continue to make sure that our education system remains the foremost one in the world.
